home_faq_what_a: {name} is an AI video generator for the Outstanding Tiny Desk meme. Pick who sings lead, plays sax, keys or backup, add a photo for each, and get the viral cut back with your picks in it and the song on top.
home_faq_people_q: How many people can I put in the video?
home_faq_people_a: Up to five: lead vocals, sax, keys and two backing singers. The stage starts with five dogs; swap one or all five. Spots you don't swap stay dogs, remove a dog to keep the coach from the viral video, and the price stays the same.
home_faq_cost_a: {plans}. You pay once, there's no subscription, and credits never expire.
home_faq_free_q: Can I make one for free?
home_faq_free_a: No. Every video is rendered by a paid AI video model, so there are no free renders or trials. If a video fails, its credits come back automatically.
home_faq_model_q: Which AI model makes the video?
home_faq_model_a: Kuaishou Kling 4.0 in edit mode, at {resolution}: the whole clip in one pass.
home_faq_time_a: Usually 7 to 10 minutes. You can close the tab: sign back in and the video is waiting on the home page.
home_faq_format_q: How long is the video, and what format?
home_faq_format_a: About 18 seconds, a vertical 9:16 MP4 at {resolution} with no watermark: the band, the big laugh close-up, the sax solo and the band again.
home_faq_song_a: Yes, the original track is mixed in. You also get a silent copy: if TikTok or Instagram mutes the song, post that one and add "Outstanding" from the app's sounds.
home_faq_capcut_q: Do I need CapCut, a template or a prompt?
home_faq_capcut_a: No. No editing app, no template file and nothing to type. Tap a spot on the stage, add a photo and press make.
home_faq_photo_a: A recent selfie-style shot: one face, looking at the camera, in good light, nothing covering it. Group photos, sunglasses, cartoons and heavy filters swap badly.
home_faq_celebrity_q: Can I put a celebrity, a coach or a player in it?
home_faq_celebrity_a: Yes. Coaches, players, celebrities and friends all work; that's what the viral versions do. Some public figures may be rejected. Keep it an obvious parody: no one under 18, and don't pass it off as real or use it to sell something. If the video can't be made, its credits come back.
home_faq_real_q: Are the viral coach videos real?
home_faq_real_a: No. They're AI edits of Charlie Wilson's 2023 Tiny Desk concert. None of the coaches or players in them performed at NPR.
home_faq_post_q: Can I post it on TikTok or Instagram?
home_faq_post_a: Yes, as a personal, non-commercial parody. The song isn't ours to license, so a platform may mute it; that's what the silent copy is for. Don't pass it off as real or use it in ads.
home_faq_fail_q: What if it fails or doesn't look right?
home_faq_fail_a: If a video can't be made, its credits come back on their own. If someone still looks like the original performer, we re-render them automatically at no extra cost before you get the video. If a finished video is clearly broken, email us within 7 days and we return the credits; see the refund policy. Expect a strong likeness, not a twin.
home_faq_photos_a: We use them only to make your video, send them to our AI video provider for that, and delete them from our storage within 2 days.
home_faq_npr_q: Is this affiliated with NPR or Tiny Desk?
home_faq_npr_a: No. {name} is an independent fan tool for parody videos, not affiliated with or endorsed by NPR, Tiny Desk Concerts, Charlie Wilson or The Gap Band. Tiny Desk is a trademark of NPR.
